citations.assessment: The claimant comes before Rabbi Abba. The passage gives two considerations, Dimi’s means and the claimant’s identifying sign. Heilprin summarizes the outcome.
The illness narrative, explicitly introduced as an alternate report, is adjacent to the standalone teaching.
Dimi, brother of Safra, is named in the standalone teaching about praise leading to disparagement.
The Semag explicitly limits the warning here to praise in front of enemies.
This local entry gives the same Bava Batra context and connects the Yehudah Chayyata narrative with the warning about praise.
